values.value: Of the things wired into HubSpot — native app-marketplace integrations, forms embedded on sites you do not control, webhooks, a two-way CRM sync — how many are owned by a team outside marketing, and how many would have to be re-pointed by someone else before you could switch off HubSpot?

[{"value":1,"label":"Several are owned outside marketing, including forms embedded on sites another team controls, and nobody has a full list of who owns what."},{"value":2,"label":"The main ones are known and at least one sits with another team, so cutover depends on a schedule marketing does not set."},{"value":3,"label":"A small number of integrations, all with a named owner inside or beside marketing, and any embedded forms are on pages we control."},{"value":4,"label":"Nothing outside marketing depends on HubSpot. Forms are on our own pages and the integrations we have could be re-pointed by this team alone."}]
Ask for the installed-apps list and the count of forms embedded outside their own domain.
Worth knowing before you answer: which teams own the integrations connected to HubSpot, and whether any of your forms are embedded on pages another team looks after.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/skills/10-roadmap.md — the external-dependency and risk-register framing, where integrations owned outside marketing are the items that set the roadmap's outer bound, which is the anchor this scale is now built on. RECALIBRATED FROM LAYER 1, for the same reason and by the same edit as migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/pairs/hubspot_to_sfmc.yaml: the base anchors counted integrations, and this pack now also asks for that count on the complexity axis (integration_surface, below), so a respondent met the same question twice. Complexity asks HOW MANY are wired in; readiness asks WHO OWNS THEM and whether cutover waits on somebody else. Only the scale moved — the named examples are unchanged.
